body: Social Security Act 2018 Schedule 2 definition of Income Test 1: the applicable benefit rate is reduced by 30 cents for each dollar of total income of the beneficiary and spouse or partner over $160 a week and not over $250 a week, and by 70 cents for each dollar of that income over $250 a week.

Social Security Act 2018 Schedule 2 definition of Income Test 2: the applicable benefit rate is reduced by 15 cents for each dollar of total income of the beneficiary and spouse or partner over $160 a week and not over $250 a week, and by 35 cents for each dollar of that income over $250 a week.

Social Security Act 2018 Schedule 2 definition of Income Test 3: except for the New Zealand superannuation case, the applicable benefit rate is reduced by 70 cents for each dollar of total income of the beneficiary and spouse or partner over $160 a week.

Social Security Act 2018 Schedule 2 definition of Income Test 4: the applicable benefit rate is reduced by 35 cents for each dollar of total income of the beneficiary and spouse or partner over $160 a week.

Social Security Act 2018 Schedule 4 Part 1 sets Jobseeker Support weekly rates from 1 April 2026, including $276.46 for a single under 20 beneficiary living with a parent, $324.50 for any other single under 25 beneficiary without dependent children, $384.52 for a specified 2013 transfer case, $372.55 for other single beneficiaries without dependent children, $521.52 for a single beneficiary whose youngest dependent child is aged at least 14 years, $521.52 for other single beneficiaries with 1 or more dependent children, partnered person rates of $316.97 or $334.70 when the partner has a main benefit, New Zealand superannuation, veterans pension, or is ineligible because of sanction or strike, and couple rates of $633.94 or $669.40 when the partner has no own benefit. The Part assigns Income Tests 1, 3, or 4 to those rates and permits MSD to disregard up to $20 of personal earnings used for childcare for specified single beneficiaries with dependent children.

Social Security Act 2018 Schedule 4 Part 2 sets the Sole Parent Support rate from 1 April 2026 at $521.52 a week, subject to Income Test 1. MSD may disregard up to $20 a week of personal earnings used to meet childcare costs for dependent children, and may treat income of a spouse or partner of certain applicants as the applicant's income when reasonable in the circumstances.

Social Security Act 2018 Schedule 4 Part 3 sets Supported Living Payment weekly rates from 1 April 2026, including single rates of $355.87 under age 18 without dependent children, $424.60 for other singles without dependent children, and $581.96 for singles with dependent children; partnered rates of $360.72 or $378.47 when both partners receive main benefits; $360.72 or $392.94 when the partner receives New Zealand superannuation or veterans pension; $721.44 or $756.94 for restricted-work-capacity or total-blindness recipients whose partner has no own benefit; and $360.72 or $392.94 for caring recipients whose partner has no own benefit. The Part assigns Income Test 1 or 2, requires earned-income disregards for restricted-work-capacity or total-blindness recipients, halves partnered rates and abatement for specified long-term residential care cases, and provides a blind earnings subsidy equal to 25 percent of average earnings subject to a maximum total from all sources of $581.89 a week plus $75.32 for a single person.

Social Security (Rates of Benefits and Allowances) Order 2026 clause 5 makes mandatory adjustments under section 453 of the Social Security Act 2018 by replacing amounts in Social Security Act provisions listed in Schedule 1 of the order with updated amounts from 1 April 2026. The 1 April 2026 consolidation of the Social Security Act incorporates those Schedule 4 rate amendments.
